Definition: of Latin origin; a centurion, i.e. captain of one hundred soldiers:--centurion.
BiblicalUsage: Kentyrion means a centurion, a captain of a hundred soldiers. Mark 15:39 says when the centurion saw that Jesus so cried out, and gave up the ghost, he said, truly this man was the Son of God. Mark 15:44 says Pilate called the centurion, and asked him whether Jesus had been any while dead. Mark 15:45 says when Pilate knew it of the centurion, he gave the body to Joseph.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the centurion saw what the priests missed: the way Jesus died proved who he was. I hold that the soldier's confession stands at the foot of the cross, and Pilate's question only confirmed it.
